newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah man gets life for French attache murder.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah man gets life for French attache murder.

text.p: Lebanon's military appeals court confirmed on Thursday the death sentence on a Moslem guerrilla for the 1986 murder of a French military attache but commuted it to life imprisonment.
The court found Hussein Tlais of the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guilty of the murder of Colonel Christian Gouttierre but said the crime was not politically motivated.

Gouttierre was shot dead near the French embassy in Christian east Beirut on September 18, 1986. A Beirut military court sentenced Tlais, a former Lebanese army soldier, to death in April 1994 but commuted the sentence to life imprisonment.
The prosecution appealed to the military appeals court, demanding imposition of the death sentence on Tlais.

The sentencing, which had been scheduled for months to take place on Thursday, came a few hours before French President Jacques Chirac was due to arrive in Beirut on the fourth leg of his Middle East tour.

It was the first sentence handed down to the killer of a foreign diplomat in Lebanon during the 1975-90 civil war. The murder of diplomats is excluded from a 1991 amnesty for crimes committed during the civil war.
Tlais had said during his first trial that Hizbollah ordered him to kill Gouttierre in revenge for French air raids on the city of Baalbek, a group bastion in eastern Lebanon, in 1983.

The air attacks were in retaliation for an October 1983 suicide bombing by Moslem militants against the headquarters of the French contingent of the multinational force in Beirut which killed 58 French paratroopers.
Tlais told the court before it issued its verdict on Thursday that it should put on trial instead the French pilots "who killed our people in Baalbek".
He added: "The crime I committed was only a reaction to the raids by the French on Baalbek because they bombarded our people".
Dozens of Westerners were held hostage -- some were killed -- in Lebanon in the 1980s by clandestine groups believed linked to Hizbollah. Hizbollah has denied involvement in hostage-taking.
